name: Baklava
about: A sweet layered pastry of thin dough, nuts, and syrup. Beirut's old shops are known for it, and it is a classic Lebanese treat.
tip: Check the nuts and butter type, and confirm the best-by date before buying.

name: Za'atar
about: A blend of Lebanese herbs and sesame seeds, used on bread and with olive oil. It is a everyday staple of Lebanese breakfasts.
tip: Prices are often quoted in US dollars, so keep that in mind when budgeting.

name: Lebanese wine
where: Château Musar shop or airport duty-free
about: Lebanon has a long winemaking history in the Bekaa Valley. Château Musar is its most famous producer.
tip: Prices vary a lot by vintage, so compare bottles of the same year before you pay.
